summary: A common-independent set of k high spectral modes on both sides of an original-coordinate cut does not imply nonzero aggregate k-cross-volume. For orthonormal Bell pairs v_j^+=(e_j+f_j)/sqrt(2), v_j^-=(e_j-f_j)/sqrt(2), all eigenvalues +1, the plus modes are simultaneously left/right independent while the total spectral packet is the identity and has exactly zero I-J cross block. For k=5 this kills the naive no-small-cover -> D5 inference. This is not a QFORM counterexample; A=I_10 is diagonal and controlled.
